not_established: The exact command line of the capture. RAIL_T0_2026-09-07.md §E2 is what the finding pins as the capture record, and it names no command: it names the rig and the sequence, in the finding's own words, 'captured by this contributor's own capture rig (delivery-incidence-study/rig, a stock @x402/fetch 2.20.0 client with @x402/core 2.20.0 and @x402/evm 2.20.0 as installed, no upgrade before the run)', and in §E2, 'Attempts 1-3 -> 200, X-Trial-Remaining: 2, 1, 0; attempt 4 -> 402.' executed_run.command records that and not a command line, because no document reachable from this record records one.
That any version-1 client ever paid the version-1 body. The body was schema-valid throughout, but no 1.x client was run against it, before or after the fix.
That any client other than @x402/fetch 2.20.0 pays the worker: one client, one language, two settlements.

That the worker's other published surfaces were free of the same class. Two of them, /openapi.json and /.well-known/x402.json, carried unrendered template placeholders on the same day, found by the contributor's own patch inspection rather than by a client and fixed in the following commit (261c48a); that is a second finding in own work and is recorded separately.

The worker version that served these bytes. The capture carries no worker version identifier, the response headers naming only a CF-RAY, and none is reconstructed here; the defect is stated from the captured bytes and the repository's commit record.

That the capture bytes are held in this repository. They are not: headers.txt and body.json are external pinned inputs in the operator's private study repository, so a reader outside it cannot recompute these two digests from this repository alone.
That this record has been independently re-run. It has not; status_label is unverified, and the contributor, the assessor and the operator of the worker are the same person.
establishes: That the Payment-Required header the worker served at 2026-09-07T09:27:34Z declared x402Version: 1 while carrying the version-2 field name amount rather than maxAmountRequired, and omitted version 1's mandatory resource and description, so it satisfied neither PaymentRequirementsV1Schema nor PaymentRequirementsV2Schema in the installed @x402/core 2.20.0 build.
That the response body beside it was a schema-valid version-1 object, so the same 402 said two different things in two places.

That a 2.x client reads the header first and falls back to the body only when the header is absent, so the worker's richer, schema-valid body was never consulted; the run failed at payload creation with 'Failed to create payment payload: No client registered for x402 version: 1', before any signature and before any network matching. No stock 2.x client could pay the worker while that header was served.

That the decoded Payment-Required header is byte-identical to the Payment-Required-Json header served beside it, both hashing to 2ab0def7270adbe95e02bd0b5ba3d05609b2b1b23138c0a574545ceca6aa273c, which cmp confirmed at capture time.

That the defect was repaired the same morning: fixed at worker commit 6e2f0da at 10:27:47 UTC, deployed at 12:41 UTC, confirmed live at 12:42:32 UTC, and settled against at 13:01:57 UTC. The served header after the deploy decodes to the version-2 shape, 502 bytes, sha256 a2a42195..., which is the repaired header and is NOT the key of this record.
